title: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness - Pre Vocational Studies - Forest and Forest Uses

subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The type of forest found mainly in water-logged coastal areas, dominated by trees with aerial roots that can survive high salt content, is known as a ________.
questions.explain: The mangrove (swampy) forest is characterized by highly water-logged, muddy soils near coasts and estuaries, populated by trees (mangroves) adapted to salt water.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which type of forest typically consists of very tall, densely packed broad-leaved evergreen trees that form thick canopies due to abundant annual rainfall?
questions.explain: The rain forest (tropical rainforest) thrives in areas with heavy rainfall and is distinguished by tall, dense evergreen trees and multiple layers of thick vegetation.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A forest area that has been degraded due to prolonged human activities like farming and bush burning, leaving fewer trees and an increase in grasses, is called a ________.
questions.explain: A derived forest was once a denser forest (like a rain forest) but has been altered or 'derived' through extensive human interference, causing trees to be replaced gradually by open grass and shrubs.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: One of the most economically valuable forest resources used globally to produce timber, paper, and furniture is ________.
questions.explain: Forest trees are logged to produce timber, which is the primary raw material for making furniture, paper, and building construction materials.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Non-domesticated animals that live and breed naturally within the forest ecosystem are collectively referred to as ________.
questions.explain: Wild life refers to all the natural, undomesticated animal species (such as antelopes, monkeys, and tigers) that inhabit forest resources and wild areas.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Forest resources such as the leaves, barks, and roots of specific wild plants are harvested primarily because they serve as ________.
options: Raw materials for making heavy machinery
Herbs with medicinal properties for treating diseases
questions.explain: Many forest plants are rich in active biological compounds and are heavily harvested and utilized traditionally and industrially as medicinal herbs to treat ailments.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: How do intact forests positively affect the natural environment?
options: By increasing the temperature of the soil
By acting as windbreaks and preventing soil erosion
By increasing the concentration of toxic gases
questions.explain: Forests play a huge role in environmental protection; the deep roots of trees hold soil together to prevent erosion, and their broad trunks and leaves act as windbreaks, reducing destructive wind speeds.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The persistent human activity of indiscriminate cutting down and clearing of forest trees without replanting is termed ________.
questions.explain: Deforestation is the mass clearing of forests (cutting down trees) for farming, urban development, or logging without adequately replanting, leading to severe environmental consequences.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which human activity in the forest is known to severely damage soil nutrients, destroy natural habitats, and wipe out slow-moving wild life?
questions.explain: Bush burning, often used by hunters or farmers to clear land rapidly, is highly destructive because it burns organic matter, kills beneficial soil microbes, and destroys wildlife and their natural habitats.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Unregulated and continuous hunting of animals in the forest by humans leads directly to ________.
options: The depletion and possible extinction of wild life species
An increase in the fertility of forest soils
The immediate transformation of the forest into a desert
questions.explain: Over-hunting (poaching) removes animals from their natural environment faster than they can reproduce, resulting in the drastic depletion of wild life populations and endangering several species.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
